{"slug": "how-to-make-your-ai-generated-site-secure", "title": "How to Make Your AI-Generated Website Secure (2026 Guide)", "metaTitle": "How to Make Your AI-Generated Website Secure (2026 Guide)", "metaDescription": "A practical, non-alarmist guide to securing an AI-generated website: what risks actually apply, what to check before you publish, and what Kodely automates.", "targetKeyword": "how to make your AI-generated site secure", "category": "Guides", "bodyHtml": "

AI website builders write real code faster than most people can type it, which is exactly why it is worth spending five minutes thinking about what that code contains before you put it in front of visitors. This is not a reason to avoid AI-generated sites — it is a reason to treat the publish step with the same basic care you would give any code going live, generated by a human or a model.

Why AI-generated code security is a real concern

The security of AI-generated code is a genuinely studied problem in the industry, not a fringe worry. Researchers and security teams have repeatedly found that code produced by language models can carry the same categories of mistakes that show up in human-written code — things like leaked credentials, unsafe defaults, or logic that was never reviewed by anyone before shipping. The exact numbers vary by study and by what is being measured, so it is not useful to quote a single statistic as if it applies universally. The honest takeaway is simpler: generated code is still code, it can still contain mistakes, and it deserves a quick review before it goes live — the same standard you would apply to a pull request from a new engineer.

What risks actually apply to a frontend-only site

Not every risk you read about applies to every kind of site, and it is worth being specific here instead of lumping everything together. A tool like Kodely generates a real Vite plus React plus TypeScript frontend — there is no backend, no database, and no server-side application logic being generated. That narrows the attack surface considerably:

  • SQL injection: not applicable. There is no database being queried, so there is no query to inject into.
  • Auth bypass: not applicable in the traditional sense. There is no server-side authentication system being generated to bypass.
  • Exposed secrets and API keys: this is the real one. Frontend code ships to the browser in plain sight. Anything typed into a prompt or pasted into a component — a real API key, a password, a private token — can end up embedded in code that anyone can view.
  • Sensitive content published by mistake: draft text, internal notes, or placeholder data that was never meant to go public.

In other words, a frontend-only AI builder has a smaller and more specific list of things to watch for than a full-stack one. That is a genuine, if narrow, security advantage — but the one risk that remains (leaked secrets) is worth taking seriously, because it is the one most likely to actually happen.

What Kodely does automatically

Every time you publish a site on Kodely, the code is scanned for accidentally-leaked secrets and API keys before it goes live. This is a mandatory, automated check built into the publish flow — not an opt-in setting you have to remember to turn on. Published sites are also served over HTTPS by default, so traffic to your name.kodely.site address is encrypted in transit. Combined with the fact that there is no backend for an attacker to target, this covers the parts of security that a platform can reasonably own on your behalf.

What is still on you as the builder

No automated scan replaces basic judgment. A few habits go a long way:

  • Never paste a real API key or credential into a chat prompt, even if you are asking for demo or placeholder data. If you need an example key in generated code, ask for an obviously fake one like YOUR_API_KEY_HERE.
  • Review generated content before publishing, especially if the site includes contact forms, embedded text, or anything pulled from a longer conversation. A quick skim of the code view catches most surprises.
  • Do not hardcode anything sensitive — internal URLs, private contact details, or draft copy you are not ready to share publicly. If it should not be public, do not put it in a prompt for a public site.
  • Use checkpoints. Every successful generation in Kodely is a free restore point, so if a change introduces something you did not intend, rolling back costs nothing.

General good practices for any AI-generated site

These apply whether you are using Kodely or any other AI website builder:

PracticeWhy it matters
Treat every prompt as if it could end up in the outputModels generate from what you give them — secrets and personal data included
Read the code view before publishing, at least onceCatches leftover placeholder text or unintended content early
Keep real credentials out of any client-side appFrontend code is always visible to anyone who views source
Use restore points when they are availableMakes it cheap to undo a change instead of patching around it
Publish to a platform that scans before going liveAdds a safety net for the mistakes a quick skim might miss

FAQ

Is an AI-generated website automatically less secure than a hand-coded one?

Not automatically. The risk profile depends on what the site actually does. A generated frontend with no backend has fewer things that can go wrong than a hand-coded full-stack app with a sloppy authentication system. What matters is reviewing what got built, not who or what built it.

Can someone steal my API keys from a Kodely site?

If a real key were pasted into a prompt and ended up in generated code, it would be visible in the published output like any client-side code — which is exactly why Kodely scans every publish for leaked secrets before the site goes live, and why you should never paste real credentials into a prompt in the first place.

Does Kodely-generated code have SQL injection or auth bypass risks?

No. Kodely does not generate a backend, database, or server-side authentication system, so those categories of vulnerability do not apply to what it builds today.

What should I do before publishing any AI-generated site?

Skim the generated code or preview for anything that should not be public, confirm no real credentials were ever part of the conversation, and use a platform that checks for leaked secrets automatically as a backstop.

Want to see the secret scan and checkpoints in action? Start building on Kodely for free — 750 credits, no credit card required. You can also check pricing or browse more guides on the blog.
